title: Constant coefficients modulo a prime as a filtered colimit of finite prime-field sums
statement: Let u be a universe, Λ : Type (u+1) any commutative ring, C : Scheme.{u} any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and p a prime natural number. Let M = Λ/(p), where (p) is the ideal generated by p in Λ, and F the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant Λ-module sheaf M on the small etale site [def-sc-constant-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. There exist a small filtered category I with objects and morphisms in Type (u+1), a diagram D : I → Ab(C_et), and a colimit cocone with point exactly F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each D(i) is isomorphic to a finite biproduct indexed by Fin n of the existing sheaf C.constantZMod p with coefficients ULift (ZMod p). No dimension, smoothness, compactness, connectedness, or characteristic hypothesis on C or Λ is imposed.

proof.text: Put M = Λ/(p). The image of p in M is zero by Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem and Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self. Thus p times each element is zero by nsmul_eq_mul; apply lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n. Restrict scalars along ULift.ringEquiv to R = ULift (ZMod p) in the coefficient universe.

Choose a basis B of M over R by the empty-set case of lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector (Module.Basis.ofVectorSpace). Its representation identifies M with finitely supported functions B →₀ R. Apply ModuleCat.finsuppCoconeIsColimit to identify these with the coproduct of copies of R. Compose the unique coproduct-point isomorphism with b.repr.symm.toModuleIso.

Directly specialize the generic Mathlib theorem CoproductsFromFiniteFiltered.isColimitFiniteSubproductsCocone to a : B → ModuleCat R. The diagram liftToFinsetObj has finite coproducts as its values and the full coproduct as its colimit point. Finset (Discrete B) is filtered: empty set gives an object and union gives upper bounds. Lean infers its small-category and filtered instances.

Map this cocone through coefficient forgetting followed by constantSheaf. ModuleCat.Colimits gives preservation for the first functor; the second is the left adjoint in lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections. Apply lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying at M and compose with the mapped coproduct-point isomorphism. Construct the required sheafification instance explicitly from limit and filtered-colimit preservation. Extend the cocone along the resulting isomorphism to the underlying constantModSheaf and transport IsColimit with Cocone.ext.

For each finite subset S, compose PreservesCoproduct.iso with biproduct.isoCoproduct.symm and biproduct.whiskerEquiv for Fintype.equivFin S. These three existing Mathlib isomorphisms give exactly the requested finite biproduct. The zero quotient has an empty basis and gives the empty biproduct. No geometric assumption enters.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring (in the coefficient universe one above that of the schemes), $C$ any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $p$ a prime number. Let $M=\Lambda/(p)$, where $(p)$ is the ideal generated by $p$ in $\Lambda$, and let $F$ be the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M$ on the small etale site of $C$ [def-sc-constant-sheaves]. There exist a small filtered category $I$, a diagram $D:I\to\Ab(C_{\Et})$ and a colimit cocone of $D$ with vertex exactly $F$, such that each $D(i)$ is isomorphic to a finite direct sum $(\underline{\mathbf Z/p})^{\oplus n}$ of copies of the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z/p}$ on $C_{\Et}$. No dimension, smoothness, compactness, connectedness, or characteristic hypothesis on $C$ or $\Lambda$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $M=\Lambda/(p)$. The image of $p$ in $M$ is zero, so $p\cdot m=0$ for every $m\in M$, and $M$ carries its canonical $\mathbf Z/p$-module structure [lem-weil-pbc-zmod-module-structure-killed-by-n]; regard it as a vector space over the field $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p$.

Choose a basis $B$ of $M$ over $\mathbf F_p$. The coordinate map identifies $M$ with the space of finitely supported functions $B\to\mathbf F_p$, i.e. with the direct sum $\bigoplus_{b\in B}\mathbf F_p$, which is the coproduct of copies of $\mathbf F_p$ in the category of $\mathbf F_p$-modules.

An arbitrary coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts: the finite subsets $S\subseteq B$, ordered by inclusion, form a filtered category (the empty set is an object and unions give upper bounds), the diagram $S\mapsto\bigoplus_{b\in S}\mathbf F_p$ has the inclusions as transition maps, and $\bigoplus_{b\in B}\mathbf F_p$ with the canonical inclusions is its colimit.

Apply the functor "forget the scalars, then take the constant abelian sheaf" to this colimit cocone. Forgetting scalars preserves colimits of modules, and the constant-sheaf functor is a left adjoint (of global sections, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections]), so the image is again a colimit cocone. Its vertex is the constant abelian sheaf with value $M$, which is the underlying abelian sheaf $F$ of the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying]; transport the cocone along this isomorphism so that its vertex is exactly $F$.

For each finite $S$, the constant-sheaf functor preserves finite coproducts, so the stage is the finite coproduct of $|S|$ copies of $\underline{\mathbf Z/p}$, i.e. the finite direct sum $(\underline{\mathbf Z/p})^{\oplus n}$ with $n=|S|$ after enumerating $S$. If $M=0$ the basis is empty, the index category has one object and the stage is the zero sheaf. No geometric assumption enters.
